script: "Every caller screams I am the enemy—why can't they just book directly?". I spent the whole day at the front desk, taking "I need to cancel" calls from people who booked through a third‑party site. Five in a morning. Why can't they just hit the hotel's own site to cancel? They're like, "How did you get through? Now you're the problem." It's the same logic every time: you use an OTA to book, you don't know the hotel's number, so you call me. Then you're like, "You can't cancel it, you're the hotel!" The audacity, bestie. (I know, right?) The whole point of OTAs is to make booking easy, but once you're in the "cancel" phase, it's like a maze. They're forced to call you, and I am forced to say, "Sorry, I can't. You have to go back to the OTA." And they're like, "Fine, fine." (Literally insane.) I am not even supposed to accept pre‑paid bookings because of all the fake "service fee" scams. That's why the OTA systems are even more confusing. When a guest calls, I am stuck with a system that doesn't let me pull up the reservation or change dates. It's like they're giving me a broken remote and saying, "Fix it yourself." (Like, what?) Sometimes, a few people are chill, they understand the system's limits, and we work it out. But the majority? They're frustrated, angry, and think I am lazy or incompetent. I am not. I am just following the rules and dealing with a system that was designed to keep them in the dark. (I am better than them, duh.) So yeah, I am fed up. OTAs exist to make life harder for front desk staff, not easier. And honestly, the average person's "IQ" on these calls is like, what? Low. (I am better, I know.)
